composition_notes: Keep the answer unresolved for the formalizer and deterministic code. Preserve all six evidence dimensions and the checksum definition. Avoid a murder-mystery framing, answer-by-title or answer-by-name shortcuts, and any implication based on paragraph order or narrative prominence.
intended_answer: The certified restoration lead is the one participant whose six evidence statuses—relational, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol—produce the incident’s accepted iterated modular checksum under the local rules. The premise deliberately does not identify that participant.
premise: At the Northbridge Conservation Workshop, a damaged illuminated map is being traced from intake through the imaging room, wash bay, paper lab, and sealed records room after fragments and repair materials were found out of place. Five workshop participants left overlapping entries, tool scans, transfer notes, and observations as the artifact moved between rooms. The provenance team must reconcile who was connected to whom, when each person handled or witnessed the map, what actions caused later conditions, where each event occurred, and the order and procedural validity of every transfer. The workshop’s incident ledger converts each participant’s relational, temporal, causal, spatial, sequence, and protocol evidence into six statuses, then applies the local iterated modular checksum and accepts exactly one resulting match. The task is to identify that participant without relying on job title, name, or narrative prominence.
setting_summary: A conservation workshop tracing a damaged artifact through several rooms: intake, imaging, wash bay, paper lab, and sealed records. Evidence comes from provenance records, access logs, observations, handling notes, and procedure checks.
target_question: Which participant is the certified restoration lead?
